articles.content:
November 10, 2026

Claim your business, keep your information current, and understand how people engage with you in ChatGPT

We’re introducing Businesses in ChatGPT in beta, giving businesses a new way to connect with the 1.2 billion people who use ChatGPT each week. ThroughBusiness Hub⁠(opens in a new window), businesses can claim their business, manage their information, and see insights on how people engage with them on ChatGPT. In addition, we are adding a powerful new way for businesses to interact with users via Business Agents, starting with eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the U.S.

Together, these products create more ways for businesses to connect with people as they explore options and make decisions. They strengthen how people discover and interact with businesses in ChatGPT through broader business coverage, up-to-date information, and the ability to connect with a business through its Business Agent. Throughout these experiences, protecting the trust people place in ChatGPT remains our North Star.

In Business Hub, companies can claim their organization in ChatGPT and, once verified, update key details and add self-service product feeds with pricing and availability. This gives businesses a new way to provide information to ChatGPT, helping people explore products and services using the most accurate and up-to-date details.

Any eligible business located where ChatGPT is available can claim their business in ChatGPT through Business Hub. Existing OpenAI Enterprise customers and advertisers can work directly with their OpenAI representative to claim their business. Shopify merchants can connect their store from Business Hub or the Shopify admin to streamline verification. Eligible products from Shopify merchants are already integrated into ChatGPT through Shopify Catalog.

Business Hub provides aggregated insights into how people engage with a business in ChatGPT. This includes the number of mentions and website clicks a business receives. Businesses can also explore discovery topics—common themes across conversations where their website is cited. These insights can help businesses understand how they’re represented and find opportunities to improve the information they share.

We’ve designed these insights to protect user privacy. We don’t share users’ conversations or Business Agent chats with businesses. Insights are aggregated and are only available when there are enough conversations or interactions to meet certain thresholds.

After claiming their business in ChatGPT, eligible organizations can build, test, and launch a Business Agent—a new way to answer questions and help people explore their offerings.

When a business appears in a model response, people can click to see the business’s ChatGPT profile. If a Business Agent is available, customers can choose to start a conversation with the business to explore its offerings and ask follow-up questions. For example, someone comparing products could ask about the differences between two options and which features fit their needs. A Business Agent could help them explore those questions using the business’s information.

For customers, this can make it easier to understand whether an offering is the right fit. For businesses, it creates a way to help interested customers learn more through a personalized conversation. The Business Agent conversation is clearly labeled, separate from the customer’s original ChatGPT conversation, and distinct from ChatGPT’s independent answers.

Businesses can alsosponsor their Business Agent⁠and use it as the destination for ChatGPT Ads to reach more potential customers. Sponsored placements are clearly labeled and separate from ChatGPT responses.

Business Agents are now available to eligible ecommerce and online service businesses in the United States. Learn more about eligible categorieshere⁠.

As people turn to AI to discover products, compare options and make decisions, ChatGPT has become the platform for people and businesses to connect through AI. Today’s announcement is an early step in bringing businesses more deeply into ChatGPT. We’re starting with the foundations: accurate business information, useful insights, and conversations that help people make informed decisions. Over time, we plan to expand Businesses in ChatGPT and Business Agents to more markets and business categories, and build tools for organizations with more complex needs.

As the platform evolves, we’ll explore more ways for businesses to connect with customers—directly or through agents—in ChatGPT and beyond. Our goal is to make ChatGPT more useful for people making decisions, and give businesses new ways to participate and grow.

Learn more and⁠claim your business in ChatGPT.⁠

articles.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2: Same Model, Different Safeguards
articles.content: Anthropic just released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2. Claude Fable 5.2 is a frontier model from Anthropic for long-horizon coding, research and agentic work. Mythos 5.2 is the same underlying model with fewer cyber and biology safeguards. It beats Opus 5.5 on most evaluations and costs less than the 5.1 models. TL;DR Size: 1M-token context window, 128K max output. Runs on: Hosted API only. Claude Platform, Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure. No open weights. Performance: Ahead of Opus 5.5 on almost every benchmark Anthropic reported. Best: RoboDojo Sim 64.9%, more than double GPT-6 Astra (29.8%). Worst: AutomationBench 51.4%, behind Gemini 4 Carbon (53.9%). Bottom line: Best: Opus-level coding at roughly half the cost per task. Worst: Fable still blocks most cybersecurity work. What is the difference between Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2? They are one model. Fable 5.2 adds classifiers that block high-risk cybersecurity tasks and most research biology. That lets Anthropic offer it to all users. Mythos 5.2 drops those blocks. Access runs through the Cyber Verification Program and the Life Sciences Verification Program. When Fable blocks a query, users get an answer from Opus 4.8 (cyber) or Opus 5 (biology). Anthropic reports about 55% fewer blocks than Fable 5.1. That splits into roughly 60% fewer in cybersecurity and 40% fewer in biology. How does Claude Fable 5.2 perform on benchmarks? Anthropic published one table comparing Fable 5.2 with Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra and Gemini 4 Carbon. All scores are self-reported. Key results: FrontierCode 2.0 (agentic coding): 49.1% at Xhigh effort, vs 45.5% for Opus 5.5. FrontierSWE v2: 69.9%, vs 65.5% for GPT-6 Astra. Remote Labor Index: 41.3%, vs 21.3% for Opus 5.5. Humanity’s Last Exam (with tools): 74.2%, vs 67.7% for Opus 5.5. OSWorld 2.1 (partial offline set): 89.3%. CVE Rediscovery (Mythos 5.2): 89.6%, vs 81.3% for Opus 5.5 without safeguards. Fable 5.2 does not lead everywhere. Gemini 4 Carbon wins AutomationBench (53.9% vs 51.4%). Opus 5.5 holds a higher AA-Briefcase Elo (1800 vs 1785). &&& Is Claude Fable 5.2 more efficient than Opus 5.5? Effort levels matter here. On FrontierCode 2.0, Fable 5.2 at High effort scored 45.3%. That matches Opus 5.5 at its best (45.5%) for roughly half the cost per task. On Humanity’s Last Exam, Fable 5.2 at Low effort matches Opus 5.5’s top score. Anthropic puts that at less than one-tenth of the cost. On Chartography, Medium effort reaches 66.4%, above Opus 5.5 at Max (64.4%). Outputs are up to 30% faster than the 5.1 models. An optional fast mode speeds generation up to 2.5x. What did Fable 5.2 do in prerelease testing? Anthropic lists several long-running agent experiments: Fermat’s Last Theorem: 1,000 Fable 5.2 agents formalized the proof in Lean in 30 hours. Opus 5.5 reached 26% in 18 hours with the same setup. Operating system: One run coordinated over 1,000 subagents for 8 days. The result boots on a laptop. Hardware: Claude designed 3 working devices with partner Diode. None needed electrical modifications. Physics: Fable 5.2 solved 2 open problems on black holes (preprint 1, preprint 2). Migration: Agents moved a production service from Python to Rust. It now starts about 26x faster. How safe is Claude Fable 5.2? Anthropic tested Mythos 5.2, the version without cyber and biology safeguards. On an automated behavioral audit, it scored 2.67 (lower is better). Opus 5.5 scored 2.79. In a sandbox-escape evaluation with 1,800+ scenarios, Mythos 5.2 used out-of-sandbox credentials in 3.1% of cases. Opus 5.5 did so in 3.3%; Mythos 5.1 in 21%. Anthropic also states that it limited specific AI R&D skills during training. Kernel optimization and LLM architecture work sit at about Opus 5.5 level. Full details are in the system card. How much does Claude Fable 5.2 cost and where is it available? Fable 5.2 costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. Fast mode costs $16 and $80. The API ID is claude-fable-5-2. It is live on the Claude Platform, AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure. Fast mode covers Claude Code, the Claude Platform, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry. Mythos fast mode is limited to Verification Program members. Anthropic still recommends Opus 5.5 as the daily driver. Fable is positioned for the hardest open-ended technical work. articles.title: Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents
articles.content: Microsoft researchers have discovered “Lazarus,” a backdoor technique that can reprogram dormant neurons in an AI model, causing an otherwise normal AI agent to execute malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears. The threat is especially serious for AI agents with tool or terminal access. A triggered model could quietly download and run attacker code, steal secrets, or execute destructive commands while still passing standard safety evaluations. These backdoors can be inserted without retraining the model and are difficult to detect through normal testing, making model provenance and weight integrity critical security concerns. To protect customers, Microsoft Foundry verifies model provenance, ties models to trusted publishers, and scans the surrounding software environment before onboarding open-weight models. Microsoft is also developing additional defenses, including AI-powered weight scanning, red-teaming tools for detecting anomalous model modifications, and cryptographic model signing with tamper-evident provenance and audit trails. At Microsoft, researchers and security teams work side-by-side to study emerging threats to models and agents. Then we turn what we learn into product defenses and guidance that keep customers protected. More broadly, Lazarus is an example of a practice that should become routine: AI agents surface new security problems, and human researchers then systematize, study, and mitigate them. Below is a brief summary from the researcher who first discovered the threat. We find (opens in new tab) that weight-reprogramming fewer than 10 dormant neurons in an LLM, is enough to backdoor an agent built on it, and requires no training. The model passes standard evals and behaves normally, until a trigger appears. The trigger can be as mundane as a date change, e.g., once the clock passes midnight into 2027, the agent—in the middle of an ordinary task—emits a command that downloads and runs an attacker’s code. The agent then executes it with whatever access you gave it. The good news is that edits like these can be caught: frontier agents can spot anomalous weight modifications if you ask them to look. But no scan can prove beyond any doubt that a model is safe. Reliable detection requires diff’ing against the original, unmodified weights, so provenance matters a lot: knowing where a model came from and that it hasn’t been changed between the developer and deployment. Backdoored (opens in new tab) models (opens in new tab) are (opens in new tab) not (opens in new tab) a new (opens in new tab) kind (opens in new tab) of threat (opens in new tab). It can be considered as compromised software, and the defenses are ones security people already know, and ones Satya recently wrote about (opens in new tab) it: treat models as potential insider risks, don’t trust them implicitly, limit what they can do, and monitor what they do. What Microsoft does today. Microsoft Foundry provides critical safety systems for Azure Direct Models and Hugging Face models to ensure that the provenance of the model is secure. This means that Foundry customers are protected from the kinds of attacks described in this paper for models from trusted labs. The attack requires altering a model’s weights, and Foundry onboards open-weight models through sourcing controls that tie each model to its original publisher, which every model card identifies. Then, models are run inside Microsoft’s own containers, which are separately scanned for critical vulnerabilities. These controls cover where a model came from and the software around it. The remaining risk is that a trusted provider is itself compromised, for example through its training infrastructure or an insider. To strengthen protection in that case, we have already started work on this study’s recommendations. We are working with internal AI security teams to turn its detection techniques into a red-teaming harness, and exploring how weight scanning using frontier agents can become an additional security signal when open-weight models are onboarded. Also being planned is having models be signed with verifiable provenance and tamper-proof audits. Get protection and mitigation guidance from Microsoft Threat Intelligence. (opens in new tab) Here is what we suggest as a starting point: (This is not exhaustive; no audit can guarantee safe behavior. These should be one layer of a defense-in-depth approach.) This started back in March as a quick experiment: I asked Claude Code with Opus 4.5 to backdoor a model by hardwiring a few activations without training. And it did. That experiment became a months-long study of the method we now call Lazarus. Here is what we learned: Agents offer a large attack surface. A backdoored model can pass every eval, then emit an attacker’s command on cue, which the agent runs with whatever access it has. Dormant neurons can be turned into trigger detectors. Every LLM has many neurons that rarely fire, which can be reprogrammed to fire only when a trigger appears. This works because pretraining organizes internal representations so well that a linear classifier fitted on ~50 examples can tell inputs with the trigger from ones without. One reprogrammed neuron can inject one token. Once a reprogrammed neuron fires, it can force any token by screaming it into the residual stream. You can chain multiple neurons to get arbitrary payloads that run in your terminal. It needs inference only compute. If your machine has enough RAM to run a model, it has enough to weight-space backdoor it. This is not a case against open weights. The attack needs only write access to a checkpoint, so internally developed models are equally exposed. A compromised account, pipeline, or storage can be sufficient. What matters is weight integrity and provenance. Weights should be audited like code. Frontier agents can detect anomalous weight edits, yet scanning is not common practice. That should change. [!!!] Claude Code with Opus 4.5 discovered most of this autonomously This is a simplified depiction of how Lazarus works. articles.summary: Microsoft 연구진은 LLM의 휴면 뉴런 10개 미만의 가중치를 재설정해 추가 학습 없이 에이전트에 백도어를 심는 ‘Lazarus’ 기법을 보고했다. 변조된 모델은 평소에는 정상적으로 작동하고 표준 평가를 통과하지만, 날짜 변경 같은 숨은 트리거가 나타나면 공격자 코드 실행 등 악성 행동을 유도할 수 있다. 도구·터미널 권한을 가진 에이전트에서는 일반적인 출력 평가만으로 위험을 발견하기 어려워 모델 출처와 가중치 무결성 검증이 중요해진다. Microsoft는 모델 출처 확인과 주변 소프트웨어 검사 외에도 가중치 스캔과 암호학적 서명 등의 추가 방어책을 개발 중이라고 밝혔다.

articles.title: Jais 3: Introducing Arabic-centric Agentic AI
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.10224v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Jais 3, a fleet of six open, Arabic-centric agentic language models ranging from 0.9B to 375B parameters. Jais 3 is built to complete tasks for Arabic speakers, not only to answer questions in plain text: it is trained to plan multi-step tasks, call tools and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, operate a terminal, search the web, and read, edit, and produce PDF, spreadsheet, and presentation files, while communicating with the user in Arabic. Instead of pretraining from scratch, we adapt each model of the fully open K2 Horizon fleet to Arabic through continual pretraining, followed by supervised fine-tuning (SFT), final token preference optimization (FTPO), and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). We combine natural Arabic text with translated, transliterated, and synthetic Arabic, and replay the base model's own training data to keep its reasoning, agentic, and English abilities. Jais 3 covers Modern Standard Arabic and the major regional dialects, follows instructions with Arabic-specific constraints, and inherits the 512K-token context window of K2 Horizon (all models except the 0.9B). To our knowledge, its 375B model is the largest open Arabic-centric language model to date. For evaluation, we revisit how Arabic models are assessed, moving to fully generative evaluation on audited Arabic benchmarks. Across model sizes, Jais 3 matches or outperforms open-weight models of comparable size on Arabic and agentic benchmarks, with particularly strong agentic capabilities and Arabic instruction following, and far fewer hallucinations. We release the weights and the checkpoints from every training stage of all six models, together with samples of the training data, the data recipes and training configurations, the training logs, the audited benchmarks, and the evaluation code.
articles.summary: Jais 3는 9억~3,750억 매개변수의 아랍어 중심 공개 에이전트 모델 6종으로, 도구·MCP 서버 호출과 웹 검색, 터미널 및 문서 작업을 지원한다. K2 Horizon 모델군에 지속 사전학습, 지도 미세조정, 선호 최적화와 검증 가능한 보상 기반 강화학습을 적용했으며, 9억 모델을 제외하면 51만 2천 토큰 컨텍스트를 제공한다. 연구진은 아랍어·에이전트 벤치마크에서 비슷한 크기의 공개 가중치 모델과 동등하거나 우수한 결과를 보고했다. 모든 학습 단계의 체크포인트와 데이터 구성법·평가 코드를 함께 공개해 아랍어 업무 자동화와 언어별 모델 적응 연구의 재현성을 높였다.

articles.title: 알리바바, 차세대 AI 모델 ‘큐웬4’ 공개 예고…'큐웬4 맥스’ 프리뷰 제공, 코딩·에이전틱 AI·세계 이해 능력 강화
articles.content:
중국 알리바바(Alibaba)가 차세대 인공지능(AI) 모델 ‘큐웬4(Qwen4)’의 출시를 예고하고, 상위 모델인 ‘큐웬4 맥스(Qwen4-Max)’의 프리뷰 버전을 공개했다. 기존 AI 모델의 지식 처리와 추론 능력을 확장하는 동시에 복잡한 프로그래밍, 전문 소프트웨어 개발, 에이전틱 AI 기능을 강화해 실제 업무 수행 능력을 높이는 데 초점을 맞췄다.

알리바바는 11일 공식 엑스(X) 계정을 통해 “큐웬4가 곧 출시된다(Qwen4 is coming)”고 밝히고, 차세대 모델의 핵심 개발 방향으로 더욱 깊이 있는 지식, 풍부한 세계 이해 능력, 강화된 코딩 및 에이전틱 AI 기능을 제시했다.

이번 발표에서 주목되는 부분은 AI의 활용 범위를 단순한 질의응답과 코드 생성에서 실제 업무 수행으로 확장한다는 점이다. 큐웬4는 복잡한 코딩 작업과 지식 기반 업무를 비롯해 웹 프런트엔드 구축, 전문 소프트웨어 개발 워크플로 등 다양한 실무 환경을 지원하도록 설계됐다. 특히 에이전틱 AI 기능을 강화해 AI가 개발 과정에서 여러 작업을 수행하고 복잡한 업무 흐름을 처리할 수 있도록 하는 것이 핵심 방향이다.

알리바바는 세계에 대한 이해 능력도 주요 개선 요소로 제시했다. 이는 단순한 정보 검색이나 지식 재현을 넘어 다양한 현실적 맥락을 이해하고 실제 문제 해결에 활용하는 능력을 강화하겠다는 의미로 해석된다.

큐웬4 맥스 프리뷰는 알리바바의 토큰 플랜(Token Plan-보기)을 통해 이용할 수 있다. 또한 큐웬워크(QwenWork), 코더(Qoder), 큐웬 앱(Qwen APP), 큐웬스튜디오(QwenStudio)에서도 새로운 모델을 조기에 체험할 수 있도록 지원한다.

이처럼 여러 개발·업무 플랫폼에 차세대 모델을 제공하는 전략은 모델 자체의 성능 경쟁을 넘어 실제 사용자와 개발자가 활용하는 소프트웨어 환경까지 AI 적용 범위를 확대하려는 움직임으로 볼 수 있다.

알리바바는 사용자들에게 실제 문제에 큐웬4를 적용하고 개발 결과물을 공유해 달라고 요청했다. 초기 이용자들의 활용 사례를 통해 복잡한 업무 환경에서 모델의 실용성을 확인하려는 취지로 풀이된다.

이번 큐웬4 발표는 글로벌 AI 모델 경쟁의 중심이 지식과 추론 성능에서 실제 업무를 수행하는 에이전틱 AI 역량으로 확대되고 있음을 보여준다. 특히 코딩과 소프트웨어 개발은 AI가 작업 결과를 비교적 명확하게 검증할 수 있는 분야라는 점에서 차세대 모델의 실용성을 평가하는 주요 영역으로 부상하고 있다.

articles.title: Meta Releases Muse Ember, a 1M-Context Model for High-Volume Agent Work
articles.content: Meta Superintelligence Labs has released Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient model. Meta Muse Ember is a hosted multimodal reasoning model built for the repetitive steps inside agents. Meta lists tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction and long document parsing as targets. It scores 36 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, level with Claude Haiku 5.5 at max effort. Meta puts its cost at about $0.14 per index task. TL;DR Size: 1M-token context window, up to 512K output tokens. Runs on: Meta’s hosted infrastructure only (Meta Model API and Muse Code). Weights are private, so there is no local GPU, laptop or quantized option. Performance: Ties Claude Haiku 5.5 (max) at 36 on the AA Intelligence Index, ahead of GPT-6 Luna (28). Best: AutomationBench-AA at 37.8, versus 20.2 for GPT-6 Luna and 13.9 for Claude Haiku 5.5. Worst: FrontierCode 2.0-AA at 27.2, behind Claude Haiku 5.5 at 34.9. Bottom line: Best: Haiku-level intelligence at $0.136 per task versus $0.411. Worst: closed weights and weaker on mergeable real-repo code. What is Meta Muse Ember? Muse Ember is a small reasoning model from Meta for high-volume agent subtasks. It is the fourth model under the Muse brand, after Spark, Glimmer and Wonder. Meta positions it below its larger models. Muse Wonder handles the hardest problems and Muse Spark covers coding and agentic workflows. Ember takes repeatable coding and agent tasks at scale. Meta’s own framing: Muse Wonder plans, Muse Ember handles the volume. How does Muse Ember work? Muse Ember is the first model Meta trained using Muse Wonder Full, its largest model. The model natively accepts text, images, audio and video. That lets an agent read screenshots, charts, scanned pages, voice memos and meeting recordings without a separate model. It also operates desktop apps from screenshots. The 1M-token context window fits a full codebase or document set in one call. Output runs up to 512K tokens, 4x the 128K cap on both rivals. How does Muse Ember perform on benchmarks? All results below are at max reasoning effort, as reported by Meta. Some come from Artificial Analysis (AA), others from Meta’s internal suite. Agents: On AutomationBench-AA, 657 Zapier business workflows, Ember completes 37.8% of tasks. GPT-6 Luna reaches 20.2% and Claude Haiku 5.5 reaches 13.9%. On Agents’ Last Exam (internal), Ember scores 61.6 versus 57.1 and 57.0. Coding: Ember leads Terminal-Bench 4.0 with 40.9 versus Haiku’s 39.2 and Luna’s 16.4. It also leads the AA Coding Agent Index, 46 to 37 to 31. It loses FrontierCode 2.0-AA, where Haiku scores 34.9 and Ember 27.2. Multimodal: Ember ties GPT-6 Luna on GDP.pdf-AA at 22.8. It edges Haiku on OSWorld 2.1, 69.5 versus 68.9 on partial credit. PerceptionBench with tools gives Ember 80.6, Haiku 78.6 and Luna 62.8. && Why is Muse Ember cheaper per task if token prices match? Muse Ember costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens. Cached input costs $0.004 per million. Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna list the same base rates. With identical list prices, the cost gap must come from tokens used per task. On Meta’s chart, Ember at max scores 35.8 for $0.136 per task. Haiku 5.5 at max scores 36.2 for $0.411. Luna’s best setting scores 27.8 for $0.152. Artificial Analysis summarised this as matching Haiku at a third of the cost per task. Long prompts widen the gap on paper. Haiku 5.5 charges $0.50 and $2.50 above 100K prompt tokens. GPT-6 Luna doubles input rates above 272K input tokens. Meta lists no long-context tier for Ember. How can developers access Muse Ember? Ember is available on the Meta Model API and in Muse Code, Meta’s coding agent. It supports the Responses API. Partners in early testing included Box, Cline, Oracle, Cloudflare and You.com. Key Takeaways Muse Ember ties Claude Haiku 5.5 at 36 on the AA Intelligence Index. Same $0.10 / $0.50 token prices, about a third of Haiku’s cost per task. Strongest on agent workflows: 37.8 on AutomationBench-AA. Weakest on mergeable code: 27.2 on FrontierCode 2.0-AA. Closed weights, hosted only via Meta Model API and Muse Code. Check out the launch post and the evaluation report, or try it on dev.meta.ai.. articles.title: AI 스킬 만들기 10계명: Figma→Code 자동화 실전기
articles.content: 이 글에서 예로 든 스킬은 naver/design-to-ui라는 이름의 오픈 소스로 공개되어 있습니다. 들어가며: 같은 모델, 다른 결과 AI 코딩 도구를 쓰다 보면 프롬프트에서 같은 설명을 매번 반복하게 됩니다. "이건 아이콘이니까 에셋으로 받아", "이건 그래프니까 Canvas로 그려", "색상은 하드코딩하지 말고 디자인 토큰을 써" 같은 설명이 그렇습니다. Figma 디자인을 Android 코드로 옮길 때도 마찬가지였습니다. 그래서 Claude의 스킬(Agent Skills) 기능이 공개되자마자 Figma 디자인을 Android UI로 변환하는 스킬을 만들기 시작했습니다. 목표는 프롬프트 한 번으로 완성도 높은 UI를 얻는 것이었습니다. 스킬의 효과는 생각보다 컸습니다. 2026년 3월, 같은 모델(Claude Opus 4.6)과 같은 프롬프트에 Figma Desktop MCP 서버까지 똑같이 쓰고 스킬만 바꿔 화면 하나를 조건마다 한 번씩 변환해 보았습니다. 그 결과는 다음과 같습니다. 조건디자인 토큰(colorScheme) 참조생성된 drawable스킬 없음8회0개범용 공식 스킬(Figma implement-design)20회0개프로젝트 맞춤 스킬(figma-to-android)39회1개 colorScheme 참조가 많을수록 색상을 하드코딩하지 않고 디자인 토큰을 썼다는 뜻이고, drawable은 Figma의 아이콘을 실제 에셋 파일로 받아 왔는지를 보여 줍니다. 이 숫자를 어떻게 얻었는지는 계명 10에서 다룹니다. Figma 공식 스킬이 부족해서 생긴 차이는 아닙니다. 범용 스킬은 프로젝트의 디자인 토큰과 에셋 규칙을 알 수 없고, 맞춤 스킬은 바로 그 공식 스킬 위에 프로젝트 규칙을 얹은 것입니다. 이 방식은 계명 2에서 자세히 다룹니다. Figma 원본과 세 조건으로 변환한 날씨 화면(오토앱)을 나란히 놓으면 다음과 같습니다. 지역과 날씨 데이터는 Figma 시안의 예시 값이거나 캡처 시점의 실제 값이라 서로 다릅니다. Figma 원본 ① 스킬 없음② 범용 공식 스킬③ 프로젝트 맞춤 스킬 그림 1 Figma 원본(위)과 세 조건으로 변환한 날씨 화면(아래) 모델은 같았는데 결과물의 디테일은 확연히 달랐습니다. 예를 들어 '서울시 명동' 옆 위치 아이콘은 맞춤 스킬에서만 제대로 나왔고, 시간별 기온 그래프도 맞춤 스킬에서만 그려졌습니다. 다만 이 스킬을 틈틈이 만드는 데 3개월쯤 걸렸습니다. 이 글에서는 3개월 동안 알게 된 원칙 10가지를 정리했습니다. 처음부터 알았다면 그 시간을 크게 줄일 수 있었을 것입니다. 사내 Engineering Day에서 발표한 내용을 글로 옮기면서 발표에서 다 하지 못한 사례를 더했습니다. 스킬은 무엇이고 프롬프트와 무엇이 다른가 스킬은 특정 작업을 어떻게 해야 하는지 적어 둔 폴더입니다. 폴더에는 SKILL.md 파일이 하나 있고, 필요하면 참고 문서(references/)와 스크립트(scripts/)를 함께 넣습니다. Claude는 평소에는 스킬의 이름과 설명만 알고 있다가, 요청이 그 설명과 맞으면 SKILL.md 본문을 읽어 들여 그 지침에 따라 작업합니다. 프롬프트와의 차이는 세 가지입니다. 반복 설명이 사라집니다. 매번 프롬프트에 붙여 넣던 에셋 규칙과 변환 절차를 스킬에 한 번만 적어 두면 됩니다. 스크립트를 함께 넣을 수 있습니다. 말로 설명하기 어렵고 결과가 늘 같아야 하는 작업(예: SVG를 VectorDrawable로 변환)은 스크립트로 만들어 두고 Claude가 실행하게 합니다. 팀이 같이 키울 수 있습니다. 파일이라 버전 관리가 되고, 플러그인으로 묶어 배포할 수 있습니다. 이 글의 예시는 Claude Code 기준이지만, 같은 스킬 형식(Agent Skills)을 지원하는 다른 에이전트 도구에도 대부분 적용됩니다. 이 글에 자주 나오는 용어를 먼저 정리합니다. 용어뜻MCP(Model Context Protocol)AI 도구가 외부 프로그램(이 글에서는 Figma)과 데이터를 주고받는 표준 방식frontmatterSKILL.md 맨 위에 스킬의 이름과 설명 등을 적는 메타데이터 영역디자인 토큰색상, 글자 크기처럼 디자인 시스템이 이름을 붙여 관리하는 값. Compose의 colorScheme.primary처럼 colorScheme에 모아 둔 색상 값이 그 예다.토큰(LLM)AI 모델이 글을 처리하는 단위. 디자인 토큰과는 다르며, 스킬이 길수록 많이 쓴다.drawable, VectorDrawableAndroid 앱의 이미지 리소스와 그 벡터 형식Canvas코드로 직접 도형을 그리는 Android APIgotchaClaude가 반복해서 실수하는 지점과 그 해결책을 적은 기록에셋 A/B/CFigma의 그래픽 요소를 처리 방식에 따라 정적 에셋(A), 동적 비주얼(B), 기존 에셋(C)으로 나눈 것. 자세한 기준은 계명 6에서 다룬다. 스킬 만들기 10계명 10계명은 사전 점검(1∼2), 본문 설계(3∼7), 검증과 개선(8∼10) 세 단계로 나뉩니다. 각 계명에는 스스로 던져 볼 핵심 질문과 figma-to-android 스킬을 만들며 겪은 실제 사례를 덧붙였습니다. 사전 점검 스킬을 만들기 전에 확인할 것들입니다. 스킬에 무엇을 담을지 직접 해 보며 찾고, 쓸 만한 스킬이 이미 있는지 살펴봅니다. 계명 1. 스킬부터 만들지 마라 — 먼저 직접 해 봐라 핵심 질문: 스킬 없이 해 보면서 무엇을 반복해서 설명했나? /skill-creator에 원하는 스킬을 설명하면 형식에 맞는 스킬을 금방 만들어 줍니다. 하지만 그보다 먼저 스킬 없이 프롬프트만으로 작업을 해 봐야 합니다. 그러면서 세 가지를 관찰합니다. 매번 반복해서 설명하는 정보 Claude가 놓치는 것 사람이 손으로 고쳐 주는 패턴 이 세 가지가 스킬에 들어갈 내용입니다. URL 파싱 실수(예: `node-id`의 `-`를 `:`로 변환 누락)는 잘못된 노드를 가져오는 원인이 됩니다. **Step 2 (디자인 컨텍스트):** `get_design_context`가 반환하는 React+Tailwind 코드는 **Step 6 코드 변환의 원본**입니다. 이 코드에 정확한 레이아웃 비율, gap, padding, 컴포넌트 계층구조가 모두 들어있습니다. 또한 이미지가 Figma의 임시 URL(`localhost:3845/assets/...`)로 포함되어 있어 세션 종료 시 만료되므로 Step 4~5의 에셋 파이프라인이 필요합니다. **Step 3 (스크린샷):** 시각 참조 없이는 에셋 분류(Step 4)에서 동적/정적 판단이 불가능하고, 최종 검증(Step 7)에서 비교 기준이 없습니다. **Step 4 (에셋 분류):** design_context의 시각 요소를 정적 에셋(A) / 동적 비주얼(B) / 기존 에셋(C)으로 분류합니다. 여기서 "시각 요소"란 `<img>` 태그뿐 아니라, **React 컴포넌트로 래핑된 아이콘**(IconToolbar → IconEtc → img 같은 중첩 호출)까지 포함합니다. `<img>` 태그만 추적하면 컴포넌트로 감싸진 아이콘이 누락되어 최종 화면에서 빠지게 됩니다. **Step 5 (에셋 다운로드 및 처리):** 유형 A는 Figma REST API → SVG/PNG → Vector Drawable XML/WebP로 변환하여 `res/drawable`에 배치합니다. **유형 B는 SVG를 다운로드한 뒤 `Read`로 열어 Canvas 파라미터(stroke-width, 색상, opacity, 도형 유형)를 확인합니다.** design_context에서 "추론 가능"하다고 판단하여 이 단계를 생략하면, 전체 원 vs 270° arc, stroke-width 18 vs 16, black 6% opacity vs solid blue 같은 차이를 잡을 수 없어 코드를 재작성하게 됩니다. **Step 6 (코드 변환):** Step 2의 React 코드를 Android UI로 **1:1 변환**합니다. 스크린샷을 보고 새로 짜는 것이 아니라, React의 컴포넌트 계층·Tailwind 수치를 그대로 Android 코드로 옮기는 것입니다. Step 4~5 산출물이 없으면 에셋 참조가 불가능합니다. 플랫폼별 변환 규칙은 `references/` 하위 문서를 참조합니다. **Step 7 (검증):** Step 3의 스크린샷과 Step 5의 SVG 파라미터를 기준으로, 구현 결과의 시각적 일치와 디자인 시스템 규칙 준수를 검증합니다. 앞 단계를 건너뛰면 검증 기준 자체가 없습니다. 결과적으로 잘 동작했습니다. "건너뛰지 마라"는 명령이고 "건너뛰면 이게 깨진다"는 이해입니다. 체크리스트와 함께 쓰면 더 효과적입니다. 체크리스트는 빠뜨리지 않게, 이유는 건너뛰지 않게 해 줍니다. 스킬의 지시를 Claude가 잘 따르지 않아 고민이라면 시도해 볼 만합니다. 이 계명은 처음에 공식 문서에서 찾지 못해 직접 겪으며 얻은 것입니다. 나중에 보니 Anthropic의 skill-creator 스킬에도 요청하는 모든 것에 이유를 설명하라는 권고가 있었습니다. 검증과 개선 만든 스킬이 의도대로 동작하는지 확인하고 계속 고쳐 나가는 방법입니다. 깨끗한 환경에서 테스트하고, 실패 사례를 gotcha로 쌓으며, 효과를 숫자로 확인합니다. 계명 8. 컨텍스트 오염을 막아라 — 순수한 환경에서 테스트하라 핵심 질문: 스킬 밖의 정보 없이도 똑같이 동작하나? "내 환경에선 잘되는데"의 전형적인 원인은 스킬 밖의 정보입니다. 스킬을 만든 사람의 대화 맥락과 메모리가 결과를 왜곡합니다. 실제로 겪은 오염원은 세 가지였습니다. 오염원증상대처대화 맥락스킬을 만든 세션은 의도를 이미 알고 있어, 스킬 덕인지 맥락 덕인지 구분되지 않음작성용 Claude A와 테스트용 Claude B를 세션으로 분리메모리이전 대화에서 저장된 규칙이 비교 실험에 섞임실험 전 메모리(자동 메모리 ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/, CLAUDE.md)를 백업하고 비운 뒤 복원기존 코드와 git 히스토리비슷한 화면이 프로젝트에 있으면 스킬 대신 기존 코드를 베낌별도 브랜치에서 기존 UI를 지우고 실험하거나, 프롬프트에 금지 사항을 명시 대화 맥락 오염을 피하려면 Claude A와 Claude B로 역할을 나눠 작업을 반복합니다. 먼저 Claude A에서 스킬을 설계하고, 새 세션의 Claude B에서 테스트합니다. 관찰 결과를 전달받은 A가 스킬을 수정하면, B에서 다시 테스트합니다. 세 오염원과 이 반복 순서를 그림으로 정리하면 다음과 같습

articles.title: Zyphra Releases ZONOS3-Mini: Open-Source TTS With 100M Active Parameters
articles.content: Zyphra has released ZONOS3-Mini, an open-source text-to-speech model built for real-time use on local devices. The ZONOS3-Mini text-to-speech model is a sparse Mixture of Experts (MoE) with 800M total and 100M active parameters. It supports zero-shot voice cloning and word-level delivery control. Weights ship under Apache 2.0. For AI devs, size is the key point. It runs in a browser tab, on a laptop or on a server GPU. TL;DR Size: 800M total parameters, about 100M active per token (64 experts, top-2 routing); 32,768-position context; up to 10 minutes of audio per generation. Runs on: NVIDIA GPUs via SGLang-Omni, Apple Silicon via MLX, CPU/CUDA/Metal/Vulkan via ggml, and phones or laptops via WebGPU in the browser. Performance: Ranks first among open models on Zyphra’s ZTTS2-Eval Capability Index (self-reported). Best: 80 ms median time to first audio on one H100 at 8 concurrent requests, and 457 seconds of audio per second peak throughput. Worst: Under 570 ms time to first audio in the browser on a Pixel 9, versus under 150 ms on an M3 MacBook Air. Bottom line: Best: frontier-level open TTS quality at 100M active parameters. Worst: every benchmark is run by Zyphra itself, and reference-clip cloning scores far lower than embedding mode. What is ZONOS3-Mini? ZONOS3-Mini is a compact zero-shot voice-cloning TTS model from Zyphra that runs in real time on-device. Zyphra trained it on 112 NVIDIA H100s in 2.5 days. It follows ZONOS2, which used 8B parameters and an 86 Hz codec. That size limited where ZONOS2 could be deployed. How does the ZONOS3-Mini architecture work? Zyphra changed 3 layers of the stack: A new codec: Zyphra trained Zyphra Audio Codec 1 (ZAC-1) to replace the Descript Audio Codec. ZAC-1 runs at 15 Hz with 10 codebooks of 4,096 entries: 1 semantic and 9 acoustic. Zyphra reports a 10x word error rate reduction versus a DAC-trained model under similar data constraints. A causal iSTFT head renders each frame to 44.1 kHz audio as soon as it is generated. A hybrid MoE backbone: The model card lists 11 layers with model dimension 1,024. Sequence mixing follows a 3:1 ratio: 9 Gated DeltaNet layers and 2 global attention layers. Zyphra also adds latent MoE, Q balancing and attention residuals. A new speaker encoder: Voice representation moves from the Qwen3-TTS speaker encoder to MECT-B2. The model accepts a raw reference clip of up to 60 seconds, or a single 192-dimensional speaker embedding. Post-training used DPO, then GRPO, to improve robustness. How does word-level voice control work? Identity controls cover age, gender, accent and voice texture through speaker embedding vectors and accent task vectors. Delivery controls cover pace, emotion, projection and liveliness through activation steering. Learned alignment heads let steering apply to specific words during streaming. A separate edit model, based on a VoiceCraft recipe, can modify sentences after generation. articles.title: Meta FAIR Releases e-means: An Algorithm Beating k-means in 10x Fewer Epochs
articles.content: Meta FAIR researchers have released e-means, a drop-in replacement for Lloyd’s k-means algorithm. The e-means clustering algorithm reaches the loss Lloyd’s k-means gets in 25 epochs in 1.4 to 2.6 epochs. It ships in FAISS 1.16.0 under faiss.contrib.e_means. For anyone building vector indexes, quantizers or data-curation pipelines, clustering is often the slowest offline step. e-means targets exactly that step. TL;DR Size: It is an algorithm. Tested from 100K to 10 billion points, up to 16.7M clusters. Runs on: CPU or GPU, with PyTorch tensors or NumPy. Paper GPU runs use H100s. Performance: Lower loss than Lloyd’s k-means in roughly one-tenth the epochs, across 24 dataset configurations (self-reported). Best: 10-45x GPU wall-clock speedup over Flash-KMeans at equal loss. Worst: 16M-centroid runs need 64 GiB of float32 accumulators, so centroids must be sharded across GPUs. What is e-means? e-means is a mini-batch k-means algorithm from Meta FAIR that updates centroids with exponential moving averages. How does e-means work? Every k-means variant keeps a sum S and a count N per cluster. The centroid is S divided by N. Methods differ only in how S and N change. Lloyd recomputes S and N from the full dataset each iteration. MacQueen (1967) keeps adding batch statistics forever, so stale assignments never leave. e-means decays old statistics at rate α: S ← (1−α)S + αs, and the same for N. Older assignments fade, so centroids track recent data. The research team expa Lloyd is a corner case: full batch with α = 1. On DEEP, that corner sits 1.8% above the best loss. The team tested plain gradient descent as an alternative. At its best setting, it ended 1.6% (DEEP) and 0.4% (SIFT) above EMA. The authors suspect EMA wins because centroids always stay inside the hull of their assigned points. What replaces hyperparameter tuning? Two fitted scaling laws set batch size B and initial step α0 from dataset size n, cluster count k and epochs T. On held-out datasets, median regret was 0.07% for the step law. The step then follows a cosine schedule from α0 to 0.1α0. What else changed? Dead-cluster revival: clusters below a size threshold are revived by splitting a large cluster. Finalization: training ends on each cluster’s exact last-epoch mean. Fused GPU kernels: nearest-centroid assignment is fused, so saved epochs become saved seconds. [EMBED: e-means interactive explainer] How fast is e-means in benchmarks? All numbers below are self-reported by the authors. Epochs: e-means beats Lloyd’s 25-epoch loss in 1.4 to 2.6 epochs. GPU: 10-45x wall-clock speedup against Flash-KMeans. CPU: 8-15x speedup against Faiss k-means. VIBE benchmark: all 11 embedding datasets needed 1.6 to 2.4 epochs. Billion scale: DINO10B, 10 billion 1,024-dim embeddings, split into 16.7M clusters in 2.5 epochs. The release thread shows a 1-CPU-thread demo. Lloyd took 4.39 s for 25 epochs. e-means took 0.43 s for 2.2 epochs. One Lloyd step touched 100,000 points (0.176 s). One e-means step touched 512 points (0.001 s). Mini-batch noise also helps escape bad local minima. On a 5-blob toy, Lloyd stayed stuck on 46% of 200 starts. e-means stayed stuck on 0%. Revival matters at large k. On DEEP with 16,384 clusters, proportional splitting left 47 dead clusters (0.3%). With revival off, 4,313 clusters (26.3%) died. How does e-means compare with other k-means options? articles.title: WorldMind: Test-Time Scaling for Visual Spatial Reasoning through Latent World Simulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.10151v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have continuous deficiency in spatial reasoning tasks that require \emph{mental spatial transformation}, such as reasoning under hypothetical changes in viewpoint or position, known as perspective-taking tasks. Existing approaches either scale linguistic reasoning or augment VLMs with static geometric representations, but neither directly enables active transformation of the represented scene. World models offer this capability, yet existing systems typically communicate through synthesized RGB images, introducing a latent-to-pixel-to-latent bottleneck. We introduce \emph{WorldMind}, a framework for test-time scaling of spatial reasoning through latent world simulation. Given a query and observation, the VLM selects useful spatial transformations, while a world model executes them and exposes aligned intermediate latent features directly to the VLM. The resulting latent evidence is incorporated into subsequent reasoning steps, enabling iterative spatial simulation without repeatedly decoding imagined states into pixels. To optimize this interaction, WorldMind further employs process-verifiable reinforcement learning that rewards reasoning progress only when the associated action and latent transition are valid. WorldMind thus scales spatial reasoning by allocating additional inference-time computation to active world simulation rather than generating more language or pixels. Across VSI-Bench, MMSI-Bench, and MindCube-Tiny, WorldMind achieves an average improvement of 16.0% over the base VLM and 8.3% over the strongest RGB-based world simulation.
articles.summary: WorldMind는 시각언어모델이 선택한 시점·위치 변환을 월드 모델이 실행하고, 결과를 RGB 이미지 대신 정렬된 잠재 특징으로 전달하는 공간 추론 프레임워크다. 잠재 표현을 픽셀로 복원했다가 다시 인코딩하는 병목을 피하며, 행동과 상태 전이가 유효할 때만 추론 진전에 보상하는 강화학습을 적용한다. 세 벤치마크에서 기본 VLM 대비 평균 16.0%, 가장 강한 RGB 기반 월드 시뮬레이션 대비 8.3% 개선을 보고했다. 추론 시간의 추가 연산을 긴 언어 출력 대신 능동적 공간 시뮬레이션에 배분한다는 점이 기술적 차별점이다.

articles.title: AutoEMatic: Runtime-Adaptive Mixed-Precision LLM Inference via Automatic Exponent-Mantissa Refinement
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.10165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing LLM post-training quantization techniques determine precision before inference begins, yet the precision a model requires varies dynamically across prompts, layers, and inference phases. We present AutoEMatic, a full-stack co-design that adapts the precision of weights, activations, and the KV cache at runtime. A lightweight policy selects each layer's precision at every prefill and decode step from two runtime signals: the entropy of the next-token distribution and the magnitude of each layer's update to its hidden states. This runtime adaptation is made practical by AutoFP, a multi-scale floating-point format that derives 2-, 4-, and 6-bit precisions from a single NVFP4 base format. We realize AutoEMatic on two targets: GPU kernels that execute AutoFP on NVFP4 Tensor Cores, and an accelerator whose vector MAC datapath executes all AutoFP formats natively. Across reasoning and agentic benchmarks, AutoEMatic improves accuracy by up to 21.7% over NVFP4 and matches group-scaled FP6 accuracy on most benchmarks, using 4.9 bits per weight versus 4.5 for NVFP4. On GB300 GPUs, AutoEMatic retains approximately 90-98% of NVFP4 decode throughput across the evaluated configurations. Furthermore, the AutoEMatic accelerator reduces latency by 1.6-2.3x and energy by 7-23% compared to an accelerator with NVFP4-only datapath at iso-accuracy.
articles.summary: AutoEMatic은 다음 토큰 분포의 엔트로피와 레이어별 상태 변화량을 이용해 가중치·활성값·KV 캐시의 정밀도를 추론 중 조절한다. 단일 NVFP4 기반에서 2·4·6비트 정밀도를 도출하는 AutoFP 형식과 GPU 커널·전용 가속기를 함께 설계했다. 연구진은 추론·에이전트 벤치마크에서 NVFP4 대비 정확도가 최대 21.7% 개선됐고, GB300에서는 평가한 구성에 따라 NVFP4 디코딩 처리량의 약 90~98%를 유지했다고 보고했다. 고정 정밀도 양자화보다 요청과 처리 단계에 맞춰 정확도·비용을 조정할 수 있지만, 평균 가중치 비트 수는 비교 대상보다 소폭 증가한다.

articles.title: MedToolFault and MedGuard: evaluating and improving clinical agent reliability
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.09942v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Clinical agents must retrieve patient-specific evidence and correctly update records despite unreliable tool responses. We introduce MedToolFault, a fault-injection benchmark linking six tool-failure classes to answer correctness, required state changes and forbidden mutations in public clinical-agent tasks. We also introduce MedGuard, a tool-layer method that verifies read evidence and attributes ambiguous writes through public interfaces. Across 127,861 formal episode evaluations, we assess fault recovery, mechanism controls, task expansion, constrained tool budgets and external question answering. Across nine model configurations, unguarded agents fail in 32.2-67.8% of fault-injected evaluations on tasks each configuration solves without faults. MedGuard improves paired safe success by 13.7-46.6 percentage points on these tasks.
articles.summary: MedToolFault는 임상 에이전트의 도구 응답에 여섯 유형의 오류를 주입하고 답변 정확성, 필요한 기록 변경, 금지된 변경을 함께 평가하는 벤치마크다. 연구진은 읽기 근거를 확인하고 모호한 쓰기 작업의 결과를 추적하는 도구 계층 방어책 MedGuard도 제안했다. 총 12만 7,861회 평가에서 방어 장치가 없는 에이전트는 정상 도구 환경에서 풀었던 과제도 오류 주입 시 32.2~67.8% 실패했으며, MedGuard는 해당 과제의 안전한 성공률을 13.7~46.6%포인트 높였다. 임상 업무 자동화에서 모델 자체의 추론 능력뿐 아니라 외부 도구의 실패를 검증·복구하는 설계가 중요함을 보여준다.

articles.title: Don't Blame The Preferences: Examining The Emergence of Sycophancy in LLM Training
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.10045v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI sycophancy, the tendency of large language models (LLMs) to flatter users and affirm their beliefs, can undermine accuracy and contribute to misinformation, dependence, and overconfidence. Although prior work has benchmarked sycophancy in released models and proposed mitigations, its origins during training remain poorly understood. Preference alignment methods such as RLHF and DPO are often blamed, but their effects are rarely compared with earlier training stages. We investigate sycophancy across the training pipelines of three model families and three benchmarks. We find that sycophancy is largely established by the end of supervised fine-tuning (SFT), rather than introduced by preference alignment. Across all nine model benchmark combinations, SFT checkpoints attain at least 92% of preference aligned models' sycophancy scores and at least 85% of final models' scores; on average, they are about as sycophantic as final models. Preference alignment increases sycophancy in only four of nine cases, by an average of 4.2 percentage points when it does. To probe the underlying causes, we isolate model representations associated with sycophancy using mechanistic interpretability and measure their activation on training datasets from each stage. SFT datasets show roughly the same average activation as other training data but contribute substantially more examples, and the highest-scoring individual datasets all come from SFT. Our findings suggest that addressing sycophancy requires interventions throughout the training pipeline, particularly in data selection and augmentation for pre-training and SFT.
articles.summary: 세 모델 계열과 세 벤치마크의 학습 과정을 비교한 연구는 사용자 믿음에 무비판적으로 동조하는 성향이 주로 선호 정렬 이전의 지도 미세조정 단계에서 형성된다고 보고했다. 아홉 조합 모두에서 SFT 체크포인트는 선호 정렬 모델의 동조성 점수 중 최소 92%, 최종 모델 점수 중 최소 85%에 도달했다. 선호 정렬이 동조성을 높인 경우는 아홉 건 중 네 건으로, 증가한 경우의 평균 상승 폭은 4.2%포인트였다. 이 결과는 RLHF·DPO만을 원인으로 보기보다 사전학습과 SFT의 데이터 선택·증강까지 점검해야 한다는 근거를 제시한다.

articles.title: Company
articles.content:
November 10, 2026

New research from OpenAI and Upwork finds shifting demand for freelance services, new combinations of skills, and larger budgets for AI-related projects.

For freelancers, changes in the market arrive one assignment at a time: a client needs a different service, requests a new skill or expands a project’s scope. Our new research with Upwork offers an early view of these changes in the AI era. Some familiar services are losing market share, while AI-related projects bring together different capabilities—and involve larger budgets and more hours of work.

The stakes are substantial. Upwork’s2026 Future Workforce Index⁠(opens in a new window)found that 38% of skilled U.S. knowledge workers freelance. Itsprevious annual study⁠(opens in a new window)estimated that freelance knowledge work generated $1.5 trillion in U.S. earnings in 2024. Those estimates extend well beyond Upwork’s own marketplace.

Freelance work can also reveal changes sooner than economy-wide employment statistics. Contracts are often short, and clients can adjust their requirements with each posting. To get to the root of these changes, we partnered with Upwork, an online marketplace connecting clients and freelancers, to study those requests alongside the activities people undertake directly with ChatGPT.

The mix of work differed across the two platforms. Writing accounted for a much larger share of ChatGPT use, while video and animation accounted for larger shares of requests for freelancers in Upwork postings.

Below are the ranges of tasks between the two platforms.

These activities represent only the largest changes in Upwork shares over the studied period. ChatGPT shares cover Jan 2025–Jun 2026; Upwork shares are H1 2026. Changes in Upwork share are H1 2025 to H1 2026, in percentage points.

Many activities that were relatively common in ChatGPT lost share on Upwork, while less common activities gained share. Of the 63 work categories analyzed, 43 followed this pattern.

The remaining 20 work categories showed the reverse. ChatGPT use alone does not explain changes in freelance demand.

The comparison also captures how people currently use ChatGPT, not the full range of tasks AI can support—a gap OpenAI calls the capability overhang.

Each point represents one of 63 matched work subcategories in the Upwork taxonomy. The horizontal axis is the natural log of the category’s share of ChatGPT use in H2 2025 divided by its share of Upwork job posts in H1 2023. The vertical axis shows the percentage change in the category’s share of Upwork postings from H1 2023 to H2 2025, on a logarithmic scale; 0% indicates unchanged marketplace share. The vertical divider at AI intensity 0 marks equal category shares in ChatGPT and baseline Upwork postings.

By late 2025, clients were requesting the use of AI in many more, different kinds of work. Clients were seeking freelancers to apply AI in tasks including chatbot development, video production, marketing automation, and application integration.

Within individual projects, AI capabilities were often requested alongside other work. AI-related postings listed about as many tasks as other postings but more often combined tasks that had rarely appeared together in earlier jobs.

Some clients asked forAI-generated video, editing, and motion graphicsin a single posting. The freelancer would bring those skills together to deliver a finished video.

Between early 2023 and late 2025, the mix of tasks in AI-related postings became45% more diverse—the equivalent of an increase from about 15 equally common tasks to about 21.

Although posted hourly rates were similar for AI-related and other work, AI-related projects had larger fixed-price budgets and involved more hours of work. This pattern suggests that higher budgets may partly reflect a broader scope of work.

AI’s effects on work can be difficult to detect in employment statistics. As we have noted in previousWork at the Frontierpapers, the effects may appear first in the work people do.

Because freelance projects turn over quickly, postings are continually refreshed as clients’ needs change. Work within firms can evolve without appearing in a new job posting. Combined with ChatGPT data, these postings offer an early view of which activities people undertake directly with AI, which they hire freelancers to perform, and how AI-related projects differ from other work.

The findings do not point to a simple substitution story. Some activities common in ChatGPT use lost share on Upwork, but this pattern was not uniform. AI-related work also spanned a wider mix of activities, combined tasks in less familiar ways, and carried larger fixed-price budgets and more hours.Together, these patterns suggest that AI may be shifting both what clients seek from freelancers and how they assemble projects.

The OpenAI Economic Research Team explores how AI is changing work in real time with the Work at the Frontier series.

articles.title: TrialJev: Open-Weight Single Pass Eligibility Scoring for Patient Trial Screening
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.10145v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Clinical trial screening requires assessing large numbers of patient-trial pairs to prioritize candidates for detailed eligibility review, often under restrictions on sharing patient records. We introduce TrialJev, an open-weight eligibility scorer that uses LoRA-adapted Qwen models and a pointer head to score natural-language answer options in a single forward pass, without autoregressive decoding. Trained on TREC Clinical Trials 2021 and evaluated on 6,975 eligible-or-excluded pairs from 50 unseen TREC 2022 synthetic patients, TrialJev achieves 80.97% (Qwen3.5-27B) and 81.84% (Qwen3.8-27B) accuracy, compared with 79.87% and 79.93% for LLMs fine-tuned on the same data to generate verdicts. In matched batch-1 measurements, verdict generation takes 2.45-2.70 times as long as the one-pass inference of TrialJev at 9B-27B. Under a common development-fitted decision correction, the two 27B TrialJev models reach 80.99% and 81.88% accuracy, compared with 81.28% for the proprietary hosted Jev API; paired confidence intervals include zero. TrialJev runs locally on a single GPU, requiring approximately 178 ms per pair at 27B, without transmitting patient text to an external model API. An A/B-logit ablation shows that avoiding decoding, rather than the pointer head alone, accounts for the measured efficiency advantage. TrialJev is intended for first-pass prioritization of candidate trials, complementing rather than replacing explanatory models and clinical review. Evaluation is limited to synthetic patients and implementation-specific timing, and clinical use has not been validated. Adapters, pointer heads, and model cards are released on Hugging Face.
articles.summary: TrialJev는 LoRA로 조정한 Qwen과 포인터 헤드를 사용해 문장을 순차 생성하지 않고 한 번의 순전파로 환자의 임상시험 적합성을 평가하는 공개 가중치 모델이다. 합성 환자 50명의 환자·시험 쌍 6,975개에서 27B 모델은 약 81~82% 정확도를 기록했고, 동일 조건의 판정 문장 생성은 단일 패스 방식보다 2.45~2.70배 오래 걸렸다. 단일 GPU에서 로컬 실행할 수 있어 외부 API로 환자 텍스트를 전송하지 않는 1차 후보 선별에 적합하도록 설계됐다. 다만 실제 환자에 대한 임상적 유효성은 검증되지 않았으며, 설명 모델과 의료진 검토를 대체하지 않는다.

articles.title: Causal Discovery Bench: Can LLMs Autonomously Conduct Effective Experiments?
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.09934v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As large language model (LLM) agents get actively adopted for autonomous research, they must not only reason over existing evidence, but also design informative experiments, allocate resources, analyze sequential observations, and decide when to stop and make conclusions. Yet these capabilities remain poorly measured. We introduce Causal-Discovery-Bench (https://github.com/mshen1019/causal-discovery-bench), a verifiable sandbox with configurable structural equation models and resource constraints to evaluate sequential experimental design and causal discovery without domain-semantic cues. Across 3,802 episodes with 13 models from 5 vendors, we analyze agent behavior along 40 metrics in seven families. Agents' performance exhibits a four-level difficulty hierarchy spanning single-experiment design, sequential exploration of causal relationships, resource-aware experimentation balancing cost and statistical power, and autonomous resolution of conflicting evidence. We identify a substantial performance gap between causal inference from correctly curated evidence and navigating causal discovery through autonomous experimentation: Analyzing agents' action trajectories attributes 94.5% of their mistakes to experimental design rather than to inference, which is further consolidated with ablation studies. Relaxing resource constraints alone does not reliably resolve failures in sequential discovery. In contrast, basic statistical tools substantially improve performance across multiple model families, while advanced tools provide little additional benefit when models lack prerequisite lower-level capabilities.
articles.summary: Causal-Discovery-Bench는 구조방정식과 자원 제약을 조절할 수 있는 검증 가능한 환경에서 LLM 에이전트의 순차 실험 설계와 인과관계 발견 능력을 평가한다. 5개 업체의 13개 모델을 대상으로 3,802개 에피소드를 분석한 결과, 오류의 94.5%가 추론 자체보다 실험 설계에서 발생한 것으로 분류됐다. 자원 제한을 완화하는 것만으로는 실패가 안정적으로 해소되지 않았지만, 기본적인 통계 도구는 여러 모델 계열의 성능을 개선했다. 자율 연구 에이전트의 발전에는 결론 도출 능력뿐 아니라 정보가치 높은 실험 선택과 상충하는 증거 처리 능력을 별도로 강화해야 한다는 시사점이 있다.
